newsitem.title: RWANDA: U.N. warns on continued violence in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: U.N. warns on continued violence in Rwanda.

text.p: The United Nations warned on Saturday that the escalating violence in Rwanda could force suspension of humanitarian operations in some areas after a week of Hutu militia attacks on foreign aid workers.

"I am surprised at the violence. I'd rather not put people in danger and if this violence continues then I have no option but to suspend operations in some areas," Omar Bakhet, U.N. Rwanda coordinator, told Reuters.

On Monday and Wednesday at Giciyi, in southern Gisenyi prefecture, two United Nations vehicles were attacked with gunfire and hand grenades and two expatriate staff were beaten up by Hutu militia, according to U.N. officials.

Witnesses said that when the two U.N. staffers were beaten up on Monday, more than 100 local people stood around laughing and clapping their hands with every blow delivered by the Hutu Interahamwe militiamen.
On Tuesday, grenades were thrown at a road construction lorry run by a Chinese company. The same day, 12 Rwandans were killed by militiamen outside Giciyi.

Last week three Rwandan civilians were shot dead and three others wounded when 60 suspected Hutu militiamen attacked a hospital in northwestern Rwanda. Two doctors from the international medical charity Medecins Sans Frontieres there were threatened with death by militiamen.
"Our position now is not to go to these areas, not to put people at risk," Bakhet said. "Expatriates and those driving vehicles are targets here, they are being shot at."

Wearing a gunbelt, black Wellington boots and British Army camouflage, he gestured at the road that runs along the open ground along the Giciyi river, a valley overlooked by wooded hills where Hutu Interahamwe militiamen operate. The Interahamwe played a leading role in the slaughter of about 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus in 1994.
The United Nations has not formally announced that it has suspended operations in southern Gisenyi prefecture but in practice no U.N. staffers are allowed to go there.
Giciyi is the hometown of Hutu President Juvenal Habyarimana, whose death in an April 1994 plane crash sparked the massacres by hardline majority Hutus.
Large chunks of the Gisenyi prefecture now are a "no-man's land", contested for in the struggle between the government Rwanda Patriotic Army and the Hutu rebel militia.
Meanwhile, in the northeastern Rwandan town of Byumba, parliament member Evariste Burakali was shot dead by an army officer, state-run Radio Rwanda reported.
It added that the shooting occured following a quarrel between the officer and a local administrator in Byumba.
